title: The 34-town search frame
caption: 33 candidate locations appear. Gola Dhoro has no accepted site point. These are index coordinates with differing source quality; no ancient coast or river course is reconstructed.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/town-axis-table.json. Counts retain repeated source and observer assertions.

title: Where the register has evidence
caption: * Required town. The categories overlap. Twenty towns have a usable modern profile, without a complete horizon error budget.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/town-axis-table.json. Counts retain repeated source and observer assertions.

title: Evidence coverage across 34 towns
caption: All eleven required towns enter the register. Thirteen towns have no horizon profile, and Gola Dhoro has an excluded profile at an unverified point.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/coverage.json.

title: Image and plan lines at the required towns
caption: A high record count can reflect several observers or many parts. It does not rank towns by evidence quality. Rakhigarhi has dating assertions but no measured lines in this register.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/town-axis-table.json. Counts retain repeated source and observer assertions.

title: The next evidence to acquire
caption: 218 town-field gaps retain reasons. The imagery field requires different products, matched walls and validated errors. Its count does not mean that every town lacks imagery.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/town-axis-table.json. Counts retain repeated source and observer assertions.

title: What north means in the measurement register
caption: 1,380 line and system records include repeat readings. An arrow labelled only N remains unspecified. A reported precision does not establish which north the source uses.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/measurements.jsonl. Records include repeated readings and source products.

title: How the 1,380 measurement records enter
caption: The 28 registered-plan records retain the plan-registration study's failed frozen validation. Repeated observers on one image do not provide independent georeferencing.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/measurements.jsonl. Records include repeated readings and source products.

title: Seventeen published Mohenjo-daro axes
caption: The Moneer axes lie near cardinal. Several street and monumental axes turn clockwise. Wanzke reports no one-sigma errors for these seventeen rows.
source: Wanzke (1987), Axis Systems and Orientation at Mohenjo-Daro, pp. 33-44. Printed p. 33 = zero-based PDF index 35.

title: Different axes within one town
caption: These diagrams compare direction alone. They do not reconstruct the relative locations of the walls. The source gives no one-sigma errors for these rows.
source: Wanzke (1987), Axis Systems and Orientation at Mohenjo-Daro, pp. 33-44. p. 33.

title: Published topographical axes
caption: The bars show the stated possible error of ±1 gon, or ±0.9 degrees. They are error bounds, not one-sigma intervals. Reported lengths range from 240 to 1,000 m.
source: Wanzke (1987), Axis Systems and Orientation at Mohenjo-Daro, pp. 33-44. p. 34, PDF index 36.

title: Other towns in Wanzke’s comparison
caption: Wanzke attributes these entries to Jansen (1979). The Harappa street span is the reported range, not an uncertainty interval. We do not pool these values with true-north imagery readings.
source: Wanzke (1987), Axis Systems and Orientation at Mohenjo-Daro, pp. 33-44. p. 34, PDF index 36.

title: The Lothal dock differs between imagery products
caption: The difference is 2.07 degrees. Bars show reported one-sigma errors. The empirical Sentinel-2 error at these short lengths is larger than its nominal ±0.30 degrees.
source: Independent verification, comparison-v3/comparison.json, /bearings/rows/1.

title: Lothal’s small turn changes sign
caption: The two nearly cardinal directions need an independently controlled dock survey. This diagram compares directions without reconstructing the dock or its dimensions.
source: Independent verification, comparison-v3/comparison.json.

title: Surkotada: the two picked wall faces
caption: These are the two exploratory picks already recorded on 24 October. The overlay retains the original native-mosaic endpoints. One observer read one archived image after seeing the earlier results.
source: Esri World Imagery Wayback release 8432. Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS User Community. Exposure date unknown.

title: Surkotada: the excavation plan
caption: The plan labels the stone rebuilding IC. Its north arrow reads N without a true or magnetic qualification. The earlier enclosure line begins in IA.
source: Joshi (1990), Excavation at Surkotada 1971-72 and Exploration in Kutch, Fig. 8, PDF index 61.

title: Why the archived Surkotada image was selected
caption: Vegetation obscures the masonry more strongly in the current image. The choice is exploratory. A release number identifies an archive product, not the exposure date.
source: Esri World Imagery and Wayback. Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS User Community.

transformation.resampling: display only; no measurement on the resized figure

title: Surkotada’s measured directions
caption: Vector lengths are 26.70 m and 25.71 m. Bearings use the retained WGS84 geodesic result. Shifting the origins for comparison does not reconstruct the rampart corners.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/measurements.jsonl. Records include repeated readings and source products.

title: Surkotada’s digitizing uncertainty
caption: Three-pixel endpoint uncertainty gives 4.96 and 5.18 degrees. Total error remains unknown. The adjacent faces share one image and one observer.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/measurements.jsonl. Records include repeated readings and source products.

title: Short segments amplify endpoint uncertainty
caption: The curve uses the same small-angle formula as the register builder. It holds endpoint uncertainty fixed and supplies no estimate of image-provider orientation accuracy.
source: build_register.py: degrees(sqrt(2) * 3 / length_px). New observations provide the two plotted segment lengths.

title: The enclosure line and stone walls have different phases
caption: A first occupation, a dated deposit and a wall-construction boundary have different roles. We retain the wall episode explicitly before pairing orientation with dates.
source: Joshi (1990), Excavation at Surkotada 1971-72 and Exploration in Kutch, Fig. 8, PDF index 61. Agrawal & Kusumgar (1973), Tata Institute Radiocarbon Date List X, pp. 579-580. DOI: 10.1017/S0033822200009024.

title: Charcoal associated with Surkotada IC
caption: These are four existing laboratory determinations. The excavation join supplies the IC attribution. The plotted ages are uncalibrated, and no wall founding date is inferred.
source: Agrawal & Kusumgar (1973), Tata Institute Radiocarbon Date List X, pp. 579-580. DOI: 10.1017/S0033822200009024.

title: Where the chronology assertions accumulate
caption: The radiocarbon assertions include repeated reporting. They contain 298 distinct nonempty town-and-laboratory-label keys, without an adjudicated count of physical samples. Seven assertions lack a lab label.
source: Q-1032 register, run-v5/town-axis-table.json. Counts retain repeated source and observer assertions.

title: Distance to the terrain controlling each model ray
caption: Distance identifies the terrain selected by this modern DSM calculation. The sampler searches from 2 to 250 km and does not reconstruct ancient obstacles or near-site vegetation.

title: A published plan of the Great Bath
caption: This is Wanzke’s Fig. 2. The plate supplies architectural context, not an additional independent bearing. The numerical axes remain linked to their tabulated source rows.
source: Wanzke (1987), Axis Systems and Orientation at Mohenjo-Daro, pp. 33-44. Fig. 2, printed p. 39, zero-based PDF index 41.

title: A site-location error changes the horizon
caption: The retained Farmana coordinate is approximate. Old-coordinate profiles remain preserved with exclusion reasons. We recomputed the modern profiles at the retained locations.
source: Plan-registration REPORT.md and Q-1032 HORIZON-REPAIR.md.

title: The deciding survey
caption: If surveyed phase-linked walls collapse onto one common axis within their errors, this reading fails. Document restorations and stratigraphic joins before reading the survey.
source: Q-1032 REPORT.md, final paragraph. This atlas spends no new confirmation population.
